title: -32001 Resource not found
summary: The RPC endpoint returned EIP-1474 error -32001: Resource not found. The requested block, transaction, receipt, filter, or state resource was not found.
likelyCauses: The requested block, transaction, receipt, filter, or state resource was not found.
The request shape, target resource, or node capability does not satisfy the method requirements.
nextSteps: Inspect the JSON-RPC method and params.
Retry against another RPC only after checking whether the request is valid.

title: -32603 Internal JSON-RPC error
summary: Generic JSON-RPC internal error. The actual cause is almost always nested in error.data — often a reverted simulation or a provider-side failure.
likelyCauses: An eth_call / eth_estimateGas reverted; revert bytes are nested in data.
The provider hit a rate limit or upstream failure.
Malformed transaction payload.
nextSteps: Inspect error.data (often itself a JSON-RPC error with a deeper code/data).
Decode any nested revert bytes.
Retry on a different provider to isolate provider-side issues.

title: -32602 Invalid params
summary: The RPC method exists, but the parameters are the wrong shape, length, or type.
likelyCauses: Address not 0x-prefixed or wrong length.
Block tag misspelled (`lastest` instead of `latest`).
Missing required field in the tx object.
nextSteps: Compare the params shape against the method's docs for that provider.

title: -32600 Invalid Request
summary: The JSON is valid but the JSON-RPC envelope is not. Check that `jsonrpc`, `method`, `id` and `params` are present and well-typed.
likelyCauses: Missing jsonrpc: "2.0".
Wrong type for id.
Params not an array/object.
nextSteps: Echo your request and compare against the JSON-RPC 2.0 spec.

title: -32601 Method not found
summary: The RPC endpoint does not expose that method. Often debug_*, trace_* or eth_newFilter on providers that disable them.
likelyCauses: Provider does not support the method (no debug/trace namespace).
Typo in the method name.
Endpoint is an L2 sequencer that exposes a reduced set of methods.
nextSteps: Confirm the method exists for this provider (Alchemy, Infura, QuickNode, etc.).
Switch to a provider that exposes debug/trace if you need them.
Use an alternative method (e.g. eth_call + eth_estimateGas instead of trace_call).

title: -32700 Parse error
summary: The JSON sent to the RPC was not valid JSON. Almost always a client-side serialization bug.
likelyCauses: Truncated payload.
Wrong content-type.
Manually constructed request body has stray characters.
nextSteps: Log the exact bytes you sent to the RPC endpoint.
Validate the payload with a JSON parser before sending.

title: -32000 Server error
summary: Generic provider-defined server error. Most providers use this for execution/simulation failures; details are typically in the message or data field.
likelyCauses: Execution reverted with details in message.
Provider-internal failure.
Rate limit or backend overload.
nextSteps: Read the `message` field carefully (e.g. `execution reverted: ERC20: ...`).
Decode any nested revert bytes in `data`.
Try a different provider to rule out provider-side issues.
